# Figures — pyALDIC-3D SoftwareX manuscript

This directory holds the figures included by `../draft_softwareX_3D.tex`.
File numbers match the order of appearance, so `figN_*.pdf`, the entry below and
the printed "Figure N" always agree.

**Current state: every file here is a PLACEHOLDER.** They are generated by
`../repro/make_placeholder_figs.py` so that `pdflatex` compiles and the layout
can be judged before the real figures exist. Each placeholder PDF prints its own
intended message and the data it needs. The generator refuses to overwrite a
real figure (it checks a `PLACEHOLDER` marker in the PDF), so once a real
`figN_*.pdf` is dropped in place it is safe to re-run.

Mirrors the 2D paper's `paper_softwareX/repro/` convention: one script per
figure, a shared `paper_style.py` (Arial, 300 dpi), output as vector PDF.

## SoftwareX constraint — must be resolved before submission

The SoftwareX Guide for Authors caps an Original Software Publication at
**6 figures**. Eight are specified below and included in the manuscript, so the
set **must be cut to six**. Recommended merge, in priority order:

1. Fold Fig. 3 (stereo geometry) into Fig. 1 (architecture) as an inset panel.
2. Fold Fig. 8 (scale/performance) into Fig. 7 (validation) as a bottom row, or
   move it to supplementary material.

That leaves: architecture+geometry, calibration, crack-aware, honesty gate, GUI,
validation(+performance) = 6. The merge also frees ~130 words of caption, which
matters for the 4000-word cap (see `../submission/00_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md` §2).

---

## Fig. 1 — `fig1_architecture.pdf`

- **Message.** pyALDIC-3D is a complete, end-to-end stereo-DIC application:
  calibration through 3D strain in one tool, with a Qt-free compute core that is
  scriptable without the GUI, and the 2D AL-DIC engine consumed as a pinned
  library rather than re-implemented.
- **Must show.** Left-to-right data flow: (stereo image pairs, calibration) →
  `sequence` → pluggable `matching` (the `CorrespondenceStrategy` protocol with
  the three registered strategies stacked as interchangeable blocks) →
  `CorrespondenceSet` drawn as an explicit isolation wall → `reconstruct`
  (undistort + DLT triangulation) → `strain3d` (plane-fit Green–Lagrange) →
  `viz3d` / `export`. Two horizontal bands distinguish the Qt-free compute layer
  from the GUI/visualization layer. The `al-dic` 2D engine appears as an external
  pinned dependency feeding `matching` only. The `.aldic3d` session file is shown
  persisting the whole state.
- **Data source.** None — schematic.
- **Script.** `repro/fig1_architecture.py` (matplotlib patches/arrows, as in the
  2D paper's `repro/fig_architecture.py`).

## Fig. 2 — `fig2_calibration.pdf`

- **Message.** Calibration is inside the application, instrumented with QC, and
  its absolute scale is verifiable — the step other open-source stereo-DIC tools
  push to an external toolbox.
- **Must show.** **(a)** A real coded circular-target board image with the three
  ring fiducials and the detected dot centroids overlaid (the detector developed
  for this work). **(b)** Board-pose coverage: all accepted board outlines drawn
  over the image frame, showing image-plane coverage and tilt range.
  **(c)** Per-pair reprojection RMS as a bar chart, with pairs rejected by the
  threshold marked. **(d)** The QC panel numbers as a table/annotation: stereo
  RMS (0.293 px), epipolar RMS, baseline (mm), pairs used/total, and the
  independent verification line — measured pitch **7.0005 ± 0.0010 mm** against
  the true 7 mm, and the baseline agreeing with DICe to **+0.06 %**.
- **Data source.** The authors' real coded-target photograph set (D12 validation).
- **Script.** `tools/calib_report.py` → `repro/fig2_calibration.py`.

## Fig. 3 — `fig3_geometry.pdf`

- **Message.** The measurement model, stated once and unambiguously: the
  conventions a reader needs to interpret every number in the paper.
- **Must show.** **(a)** The two-camera rig with the left camera as world frame
  (`R = I`, `T = 0`), the right camera at `X_R = R X_L + T`, the baseline `|T|`,
  a surface point `P` projected to `x_L` and `x_R`, the epipolar line in the
  right image bounding the search, and DLT triangulation as the intersection of
  two rays; labelled units (px in the image planes, mm in the world).
  **(b)** The three correspondence strategies as arrow diagrams on a 2 × N grid
  of frames: `track_both` (one stereo arrow at frame 1 + two temporal chains),
  `stereo_each_frame` (one temporal chain + a stereo arrow per frame),
  `ref_direct` (all frames matched back to left frame 1).
- **Data source.** None — schematic; geometry drawn to scale from the Sample 3
  calibration (baseline, stereo angle) so the figure is not fictional.
- **Script.** `repro/fig3_geometry.py`.

## Fig. 4 — `fig4_crack_aware.pdf`

- **Message.** Contribution (ii): a discontinuous surface field is *measured*,
  not smoothed across. This is the figure that must convince a mechanics reader.
- **Must show.** One frame of a cracked specimen, three panels on a **shared**
  colour scale: **(a)** the ROI with the thin barrier cut along the crack,
  overlaid on the reference frame; **(b)** the naive result — strain computed
  with an ordinary plane-fit neighbourhood, showing the artificial smear that
  bridges the two crack faces; **(c)** the crack-aware result — the same run with
  the barrier honoured, so no neighbour pair crosses it, the crack band is
  blanked by the trim mask, and the two faces carry their own strain.
  **Inset:** a line profile of `eyy` perpendicular to the crack in (b) and (c) on
  the same axes, showing the naive curve rounding the jump.
- **Data source.** A cracked-specimen stereo pair (authors' data) + two runs of
  the same session with the barrier disabled/enabled.
- **Script.** `repro/fig4_crack_aware.py`.

## Fig. 5 — `fig5_honesty_gate.pdf`

- **Message.** Contribution (iii): an independent re-verification of the
  *shipped* displacement catches silent solver failures that a conventional
  pipeline reports as valid.
- **Must show.** **(a)** Per-frame ZNSSD of the shipped cumulative displacement
  — evaluated by re-sampling the reference subset at the reported deformed
  position, independently of the solver's own objective — for two runs on the
  same data: a healthy run (flat, low) and a run whose accumulative warm start
  froze (flat displacement, but ZNSSD rising past the gate threshold). Draw the
  gate threshold (1.0, i.e. ZNCC 0.5) as a horizontal line and mark the first
  flagged frame. **(b)** The displacement field at the flagged frame for both
  runs, showing that the frozen run *looks* plausible. **(c)** The per-frame
  validity-fraction ledger as the GUI log reports it, for the same two runs.
- **Data source.** `tools/matlab_parity.py` P2 gate output (the 0.38 / 0.43 px
  template-matching truth comparison) plus a deliberately frozen-warm-start run
  reproducing the historical failure.
- **Script.** `repro/fig5_honesty_gate.py`.

## Fig. 6 — `fig6_gui.pdf`

- **Message.** The workflow is complete and GUI-driven; no scripting and no
  external calibration tool is required.
- **Must show.** A full-window screenshot of the three-column main window on a
  real stereo dataset, annotated **(i)** left workflow sidebar (Images with the
  two L/R drop zones, Calibration, Workflow Type, Initial Guess, Region of
  Interest, Parameters, Advanced), **(ii)** centre canvas with the ROI and the
  colour-mapped `W` field over the speckled specimen, **(iii)** right sidebar
  (Run, progress + ETA, field selector, colormap/range/opacity, units, 3D View
  launcher, console log). Insets: the interactive PyVista **3D View** window and
  the **Strain Post-Processing** window. All fonts must be legible at print size
  — capture at high DPI, do not downscale.
- **Data source.** `examples/Images_Stereo_Sample3_images` (Stereo-DIC Challenge
  1.0 Sample 3) or the authors' real tension dataset.
- **Script.** `tools/gui_screenshot.py` (offscreen, `QT_QPA_FONTDIR` set) +
  `repro/fig6_gui.py` for the annotation layer.

## Fig. 7 — `fig7_validation.pdf`

- **Message.** The port is correct: it reproduces the published MATLAB reference
  implementation and independent community benchmarks.
- **Must show.** **(a–c)** Node-wise scatter of pyALDIC-3D vs the MATLAB
  3D-Stereo-ALDIC reference on Stereo-DIC Challenge 1.0 Sample 3, frame 0→1, one
  panel each for `U`, `V`, `W`, with the 1:1 line, the fitted regression slope
  (≈ 1.0) and R². **(d)** Histograms of the node-wise `|difference|` with the
  medians annotated (U 1.3 µm, V 1.0 µm, W 6.0 µm; shape Z 29.7 µm).
  **(e)** Challenge 2.0 Task 1: the `eyy` profile against the published anchor
  (0.269 % measured vs 0.26 %) and the 0.003–0.015 px agreement with DICe.
- **Data source.** `tools/matlab_parity.py` (P1 gate),
  `tools/challenge_c2_task1.py`, `tools/challenge_s2.py`, `tools/challenge_s4.py`.
- **Script.** `repro/fig7_validation.py` (reads the parity/challenge NPZ dumps).

## Fig. 8 — `fig8_scale.pdf`

- **Message.** Contribution (iv): the application survives real experimental
  campaigns — long sequences at full sensor resolution, on a workstation, with
  no drift.
- **Must show.** **(a)** Peak resident memory vs frame index for the two stress
  runs (150 frames × 12 Mpx → 5.68 GB peak; 400 frames × 5 Mpx → 3.06 GB),
  demonstrating that lazy streaming keeps memory flat rather than growing with
  sequence length; the pre-run projections (4.63 / 2.45 GB) marked.
  **(b)** Per-frame tracking time (median 1.02 s/frame on the 400-frame run) as a
  time series, showing no degradation. **(c)** End-frame accuracy against the
  synthetic ground truth vs frame index (image-plane 0.010–0.011 px, 3D point
  0.002–0.004 mm), demonstrating no drift over 400 frames. **(d)** Bar chart of
  the two kernel speedups: strain kernel 6.5–19× (Numba vs array reference,
  agreement < 1e−9) and verification gate 3.29× (bit-identical verdicts,
  max |diff| = 0 over 275,184 values).
- **Data source.** `tools/stress_test.py` / `tools/stress_synth.py` run logs (G4)
  and `tools/bench_strain3d.py`.
- **Script.** `repro/fig8_scale.py`.
